about: Every feature of Freally OS, one tagged spec each, driven over CDP by tools/cdp-runner. A feature without a spec, or a spec without a feature, fails the run.

features.what: The bootloader verifies the signed image and paints Freally OS vX.Y.Z in Noto Sans: the whole screen, pixel for pixel (an image without stage, so the title stays).
One flipped bit in the image gets the integrity screen, with the reason, and nothing from the image runs.
A release bootloader boots its staging-signed release image.
A release bootloader refuses a dev-signed image: a key this computer doesn't trust.
Boot services exit, the runtime services move to the direct map, and Freally Core is entered with a BootInfo it accepts, then paints its screen; the boot reaches stage's first frame.
A kernel fault stops on the panic screen in Noto, naming the exception, its RIP and the machine state, drawn exactly as the kernel logs it.
A kernel panic survives a warm reboot: the next boot finds the last-panic page, files it as a fault report from freally-core, and logs it once.
Freally Core starts conductor from the image as PID 1, its ELF re-checked and loaded W^X; conductor says it started and C0 is stamped.
The logger keeps every service's lines and the kernel's own, mirrors services' lines to COM1 in dev and e2e, and reads them back page by page.
Conductor starts services from their manifests; each one that restarts is killed in turn and is back within 200 ms.
devmgr reads the firmware's ACPI tables and finds every PCI function through MCFG's configuration space: exactly QEMU's own list.
drv-gop-fb offers the firmware's framebuffer as a write-combining VMO; filled with the UI kit's ground, the screen is that colour, every pixel.
Every printable character and modifier typed reaches drv-i8042 through IRQ 1 as scan code set 2 and comes out as the right Freally key code and US character.
The PS/2 mouse, found with its IntelliMouse wheel, reports through IRQ 12 every movement on both axes, each of its three buttons, and the wheel both ways, in HID's directions.

Stage's windows on the real screen: opened centred and cascaded, raised and focused by a press, moved by their strip, Alt+Tab, Alt+F4 and the close button, keys to the focused window only, in both themes.

The fleet cursor from stage's first frame: the ring round the dot following the real mouse, bigger with a faint fill over the close button, smaller while held, the I-beam (and no ring) where a window asks for text.
Screenshots and injected input for the Brain and cdpd only; a window's accessibility tree kept; the UI scale reaching stage and every window, the strip growing with it, off-step scales refused.

The Rack along the foot, stamped S4: the launcher, Terminal and Monitor keys from the hardware set (apps not in the image at 40 %), their LEDs, the 12-hour clock in its well; a key's tooltip after 600 ms, gone when the pointer leaves; the launcher key opens the launcher.
Super opens the launcher, 560 px wide, centred 30 % down, focused; typing filters it; Esc and Super close it; Super+T starts Terminal.

A recorded session (16/256/truecolor, the attributes, cursor placing, erasing, wrapping, a scroll region, the title, the alternate screen) leaves the screen it leaves on the host: the text read back, the pixels compared; the real keyboard reaches the shell.
Every built-in runs in the terminal and says what it should; each answers --help; mistakes say how; restart isn't in an e2e image; theme and scale reach stage; line editing and history.

cdpd's methods through cdp-host: the targets, the processes (conductor first), the boot timeline, the faults, readBack of stage's theme, the metrics and the Log domain, each agreeing with the real services.

The apps as a document: the Rack's keys, Monitor's tabs and sort headers, the launcher's search and rows (a click on one starts its app), the terminal's screen. Each found by a selector, worked by its box with the real mouse and keyboard, read back from its attributes and the app; the AX tree agrees.

The sweep over the desktop: every Rack key (the launcher's opens the launcher; each app's starts it), every launcher row (a click starts its app), the search (its value is what's typed; "zz" leaves no rows).

The sweep over Monitor: every tab selected; every sort header pressed, sorting, and the other way on a second click; every fault row opened and closed; every log chip moving the filter on. Each read back from its tree and Monitor's door.

Everything without a pointer: Super, typing and Enter start Monitor; Tab and Shift+Tab walk its controls (the tree and the ring say which has focus) and Enter and Space work them (sorts, tabs, chips); Super+T and typing reach the shell; Alt+Tab moves between windows; Alt+F4 closes them.

Every surface in light, then dark: the ground, the Rack, the launcher, Monitor and the terminal in their theme's tokens; each title strip follows the theme the moment it changes (lit when focused, dimmed when not). Pictures of both kept.

Super+M opens Monitor; Processes lists every service with its state, memory, CPU % and restarts, sorted by a header click and back; Boot shows every stage and the summary; Faults says what crashed; Log is live and its chips filter it; Ctrl+Tab steps the tabs.
On a machine with no PS/2 controller, drv-i8042 says No PS/2 controller found. and ends cleanly: never restarted, nothing else disturbed.
Bytes through COM3 and back without losing one, while the door stalls so the driver must hold the line: 256 KB each run, 10 MB with --slow.
A command sent the moment the VM restarts, before the serial driver or the door exists, is still answered: nothing that arrives before a client opens the port is lost.
Conductor's boot line holds every stage B0 to S3 in order, B0 at 0, and the firmware's own times (or that there's no FPDT).
Slot B on trial with an image that crashes before conductor: three trial boots, then the fourth lands on slot A, and the log says the update didn't start.
Slot B on trial with a good image: it boots with a try spent, and conductor marks it Good through UEFI SetVariable 10 s after every boot service is running.
On a 16-inch 2560×1600 panel (the stand-in EDID, since a VM's firmware gives none) the bootloader sets the panel's own mode and stage starts at 150 %: the screen is 2560×1600.

Monitor → Devices: every CPU with its core type (TASK-070), the framebuffer and display controller to drv-gop-fb, the PS/2 controller to drv-i8042, COM2 and COM3 to drv-uart16550, an unclaimed device with —; the wheel and keys scroll it, never past either end.

The kernel panics (the e2e door's kernel panic, syscall 38, e2e kernels only); after a warm reboot Monitor → Faults lists it from the last-panic page as freally-core's Panic in the last boot, with what it said.
A dev image booted with log=screen (CMDLINE.TXT on the stick) and no stage shows the log on its own screen, the kernel's early lines included: the green heading and the lines under it.
With stage in the image, the logger draws the log only until stage begins, says so, and the desktop is what shows.
Idle for the time set, the screensaver (Bounce) starts over everything: the Rack and the cursor are gone from the screen.
A key ends the screensaver and does nothing else: Super, which opens the launcher, doesn't; the next Super does.
With Reduce Motion, the screensaver is the F still and dimmed: two frames a second apart are the same.
Bounce at 2560x1600: the F glides with its glow, and the desktop draws at least 30 frames a second.
The turning block at 2560x1600: the block of black glass turns with the F on its faces, at least 30 frames a second.
Swarm at 2560x1600: the sparks flock into the F, at least 30 frames a second.
Warp at 2560x1600: the tunnel of green light, Fs streaking past, at least 30 frames a second.
A whole GPT disk on NVMe (ESP, FREALLY_SYSTEM_A and _B, FREALLY_DATA): the bootloader reads the table through BlockIo, boots slot A from its partition, and the desktop comes up.
On the GPT disk, a slot B that crashes in trial three times falls back to slot A, both read from their partitions.

drv-nvme on the NVMe disk: Identify, the GPT read, a write to block 0 refused by the partition interlock (AccessDenied) before the controller sees it, a block of FREALLY_DATA written, flushed and read back.
Memory a program frees is given back: forty calls to conductor from the Terminal leave its memory where it was, within 64 KiB.
Through the Terminal, fstd::fs, vfs, ffs and drv-nvme: a folder made, a file written, read, moved and removed in the session's home; / and /system listed.
Another account's home is AccessDenied and not listed in /home; /system is read-only; with no session, no home.
A file written and synced is there after the machine resets mid-session; the mount after it runs ffsck, clean.

On a disk with no accounts, Welcome is up and the desktop locked: Enter walks the fields, every mistake said under its field, the name fills the username, a click focuses, both themes; Create account makes the Owner, logs it in, and the desktop is theirs.
Logged out, Login over the dimmed wallpaper: a wrong password said and the well emptied; arrows and clicks choose an account; Tab reaches Shut down and Restart; both themes; Log in opens the desktop.
PRD § 7: Login → desktop ≤ 1 s, Argon2id included, from Enter in the password well to the desktop saying whose it is.

Every Personalisation control worked and read back from stage: the theme and the four backgrounds live, the clock, screensaver, idle time, Reduce Motion and scale only at Apply (the window made again at 125 %); Escape and Cancel put back what was live; OK saves and closes; the look comes back at the next login; Restore Defaults.
The tab list one stop, its arrows cycling (Home, End); each row one stop, worked by its keys; Tab reaches OK and Cancel and comes round; Shift+Tab back; Escape cancels.

Accounts lists who is here; Add an account (a mismatch said under its field), Change your password (a wrong one said; changed and back), Export, Import from the list (opened, previewed, renamed), Remove (the username typed exactly); the Owner has no Remove.
The home listed, folders first, sizes in words; a folder opened by double-click and by Enter; Backspace and Up back to the home with the folder it left chosen; the grid and back.
A new folder named as it is made; F2 renames (an empty name and a taken one refused, Escape leaves it); Delete to the bin, Restore, Empty the bin for good.
A row dragged onto a folder in its own window moves into it; Ctrl+N opens a second window; a row dragged onto the other window (stage carries it) moves into the folder it shows; Alt+F4 closes each.
Restart from Login: ffs unmounts cleanly, the machine restarts, mounts without ffsck, and Login is up again.
Shut down from Login by the mouse: ffs unmounts cleanly and the machine powers off through the firmware (QEMU exits).

On a disk with no accounts the first made is the Owner; bad names and short passwords refused; a wrong password says so; logged in, the home is the session's (written and read in the Terminal); logged out, shut; only the Owner, with its password, adds another, whose home is its own.
US-015: from the third wrong password in a row, each makes the next try wait a second more, the right password included; a success starts the count again.
A password change needs the old one; after it the old one is refused and the new one opens the same home with its files, before and after the machine resets.
FR-046: a scan of all guest RAM (QMP pmemsave) finds the account's master key while it's logged in and nowhere after logout.
US-016: the session's home sealed with its re-typed password into Exports/<user>.facct (Exports left out); a wrong password refused; the bundle listed; its preview opens only with the password.
FR-047: a bundle made into an account: the same username refused and named, a wrong password refused, renamed by the Owner it is made, its files there under the bundle's password, without Exports.
Every UI scale 100-300 %: stage and the desktop take the art made for it, the title strip is its own pixels, nothing drawn larger than it is or from another scale (the crisp guard).
